title: An electric wire took his arm at 8. He won Paralympic gold at 23. And again at 35. October 14, 2026.
excerpt: From a home Games where India finished 2nd for the first time ever, to a Pulitzer-winning comic about a uniquely Indian scam, to a doctor who gave her entire savings back to the hospital that trained her - October 14's five stories are about turning a setback, or a debt, into a defining move.
bodyHtml:
Today's five stories share an odd thread: every one of them is about someone converting a loss, a debt, or an underdog position into the thing they're remembered for - a badminton gold on the final point, a scam story told in illustration rather than text, a life savings sent back to where it started, a defence sector that used to import and now exports, and a javelin thrower who turned one lost arm into two Paralympic golds, twelve years apart.

October 14, 2010: India finished 2nd on a Commonwealth Games medal table for the first time ever

The Delhi Commonwealth Games closed with India in second place overall - 38 gold medals, 101 total - for the first time in the event's history. The clinching gold came on the very last day, when Saina Nehwal saved a match point to win the women's badminton singles final.

A comic-style investigation into a scam that traps Indians by phone just won a Pulitzer Prize

Anand RK and Suparna Sharma won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Illustrated Reporting and Commentary for 'trAPPed,' a graphic investigation into India's 'digital arrest' scam phenomenon, published with Bloomberg's Natalie Obiko Pearson.

A US doctor just gave her entire life's savings to the hospital that trained her

Dr. Uma Devi Gavini, an immunologist who left Guntur Medical College for the US in 1965, pledged roughly Rs 20 crore of her savings to fund a new mother-and-child care block at the government hospital where she trained.

India's defence production just hit a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore

India's defence production reached an all-time high of Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, up 15.6% year-on-year. The private sector's share of that output rose to 24%, about Rs 42,000 crore, up from 22% the year before.

An electric wire took his arm at 8. He won Paralympic gold at 23. And again at 35

Devendra Jhajharia lost his left arm as a child after touching a live 11,000-volt wire while climbing a tree in his Rajasthan village. He won javelin gold at the 2004 Athens Paralympics, won gold again at Rio 2016 - breaking his own record - and added a silver at Tokyo 2021.

Five stories, one pattern: a final-day gold, a scam turned into prize-winning art, a debt of gratitude repaid in full, a sector that flipped from importer to exporter, and one lost arm that produced two Paralympic golds across three decades.
